name: Formal script
summary: Joined, sloped letters from the pointed pen of the eighteenth-century writing master. Pressure makes the downstrokes swell and the upstrokes become hairlines. It speaks of invitations, ceremony and romance, and reads well only in short lines.

philosophy.core_thesis: A letter is one movement of a flexible pointed pen: pressure on the downstroke, a hairline on the upstroke, and every letter joined to the next.
design_principles: Slope the letters 50–55° from the baseline, at one constant angle.
Swell the downstrokes and keep the upstrokes and the joins as hairlines.
Join each lower-case letter to the next with a hairline that leaves from the baseline or the x-height.
Keep the x-height small, 0.40–0.60 of the cap height, so the loops of the ascenders and descenders have room.
Make the capitals large, with oval loops and one or two flourishes, and never set a word in them.
Set the text with no letter spacing, so the joins meet.
anti_patterns: Positive tracking that breaks the joins
Fake slope made by the software on an upright face
Script and blackletter in one line

classification.note: Vox-ATypI puts joined, formal scripts here; unjoined hand letters go to Manual (Graphic) or to DIN Gruppe IX, Handschriftliche Antiqua.

anatomy.contrast: Strong: the downstrokes swell to 3–8 times the hairline upstrokes.
anatomy.stress: Along the slope of the letter, 50–55° from the baseline.
anatomy.serifs: No serifs: the strokes start and end in hairlines, loops or small ball terminals.
anatomy.terminals: Hairline entry and exit strokes, loops on b, d, h, k and l, and ball ends on capitals.
anatomy.aperture: Closed, oval counters along the slope.
anatomy.key_letters: A looped l and h, an r with a shoulder hook, an s with a closed loop, and capitals with large oval flourishes.

metrics.x_height: The x-height is 0.40–0.60 of the cap height; the loops above and below take most of the line.
metrics.contrast: The o test gives only 1.0–2.0, because it measures on the vertical and the horizontal while the stress follows the slope of the letter.
metrics.width: Narrow: the mean advance of a to z is 0.30–0.42 em, because the letters lean and overlap.
metrics.figures: Old-style or lining figures with the same slope and hairlines.

setting.text_sizes: Do not use it below 18 pt or 24 px; the hairlines break up.
setting.display_sizes: Set names, titles and short phrases at 28–120 pt.
setting.leading: Set the leading at 1.3–1.6, so the loops of one line do not hit the next.
setting.tracking: Set 0 em; never letter-space a joined script.
setting.case_and_features: Use upper and lower case, and the contextual alternates and swashes of the font for the first and last letters.

pairing.rule: Use the script for one line only and pair it with an upright face of high contrast or with spaced capitals of a serif.

pairs.role: upright serif for details and text
pairs.why: Both have strong thick and thin contrast from the same engraved tradition.

pairs.role: spaced capitals for names and dates
pairs.why: Baskerville was a writing master too, so the forms agree.

reference_faces.note: The Universal Penman is a book of engraved copperplates, not metal type; the first metal scripts tried to copy those plates.

evidence.title: The Universal Penman, a plate of engraved roundhand
evidence.credit: Engraved by George Bickham; scan on Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Grace and ceremony: the reader feels a personal, formal occasion.

use_cases: one signature line in a brand
avoid_when: The text is longer than one or two lines.
The text is under 18 pt or 24 px.
The brief asks for a technical or neutral voice.

modifiers.how: Set the line in the italic of a transitional serif; keep the slope and the contrast, drop the joins.
Pair the script with a Didone title in capitals and widen the white space.

x_height_ratio.note: Many scripts have an x-height below 0.35; the domain floor clips the range.

stroke_contrast.note: The o test misleads here; the value is the stem against the hairline.

tracking.note: Tracking breaks the joins of a connected script.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 4th ed. 2012)
